primary.title: Corpus Juris Civilis
primary.author: Justinian I
primary.rationale: The Corpus Juris Civilis is the most significant legal work of Justinian I, representing the codification and organization of Roman law. It is a foundational text for Western legal systems.

primary.title: Novellae Constitutiones
primary.author: Justinian I
primary.rationale: These are the later laws issued by Justinian after the initial codification of the Corpus Juris Civilis. They represent his ongoing legislative efforts and provide insight into the later period of his reign.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to the Age of Justinian
secondary.author: Michael Maas
secondary.rationale: This is a comprehensive collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Justinian's reign, including politics, religion, law, and culture. It is a standard academic reference.

secondary.title: Justinian's Flea: The Flea Plague and the Fall of Constantinople
secondary.author: William Rosen
secondary.rationale: While focusing on a specific event, this book provides a detailed narrative of Justinian's era and his impact, drawing on historical sources and scholarly analysis.

secondary.title: The Making of the Christian Middle Ages
secondary.author: R.A. Markus
secondary.rationale: This work places Justinian's reign within the broader context of the transition from the Roman Empire to the early Middle Ages, examining his religious policies and their long-term consequences.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources for Justinian I are primarily legal texts and imperial constitutions. Direct personal writings are rare. The Corpus Juris Civilis is often published in multiple editions and translations, making it accessible through various academic libraries and digital archives.
